technical_and_design_decisions: Implement Teradata support using Sqoop's connection-manager extension point and add a Teradata connection manager that supports the JDBC URL, driver, credentials, and import configuration shown in U1.
Make the logging directory configurable through an explicit property with a backward-compatible default of ${xd.home}/logs.

Extract message-bus functionality and serialization codecs into reusable Spring Bus Maven modules, preserving existing public APIs where practical and updating Spring XD to consume them as dependencies.
Move input/output type-conversion functionality into Spring Cloud Data Flow as a reusable module, with extension points for custom domain-object converters.
Implement the single-node XD Admin SPI using the existing Module Launcher in-process, with lifecycle management, status reporting, and local transport abstractions.
Implement the Diego Receptor XD Admin SPI as an adapter around the Receptor HTTP/API model, translating module launch, status, shutdown, and failure operations into the existing XD Admin SPI.

Treat service-discovery self-registration as an investigation and working proof of concept rather than a production-grade implementation, documenting protocol, lifecycle, configuration, and compatibility findings.
Use Maven dependency management and compatibility shims where required to minimize breaking changes to existing Spring XD modules.
Add automated unit, integration, and regression tests for changed behavior, using mocks or embedded infrastructure where external Teradata, Diego, or service-discovery systems are unavailable.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD, Spring Bus, Spring Cloud Data Flow, Sqoop, and Module Launcher codebases are available and buildable, and the developer has access to the relevant repositories.
The increment targets the historical technology versions implied by the specification rather than upgrading the entire platform to current Spring Framework versions.
Existing Sqoop APIs provide sufficient extension points for a Teradata connection manager; implementing or modifying the Teradata JDBC driver itself is out of scope.
A licensed or otherwise available Teradata JDBC driver can be used for tests, but the driver binary and Teradata database administration are not part of the implementation effort.
The logging configuration change must preserve the current default path and support configuration through the established XD property/configuration mechanism.
The repository moves retain behavior and public contracts unless a package or dependency change is required; downstream migration support is limited to updating the in-scope projects.
The single-node implementation is intended for local development and functional pipeline use cases, not high availability or production-scale scheduling.
The Diego Receptor implementation targets the documented Receptor/API capabilities available at the time of the increment and does not include a full Cloud Foundry deployment automation effort.
U8 requires a feasibility investigation, architecture recommendation, and representative self-registration prototype with tests, not a complete production service-discovery platform.

Effort includes coding, code review preparation, automated tests, local integration validation, build updates, and documentation, but excludes project management, external vendor support, and elapsed waiting time.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing XD, Sqoop integration, message-bus, codec, conversion, Module Launcher, SPI, build, test, and configuration structures; identify extension points, dependency boundaries, compatibility constraints, and acceptance-test locations.

Implement and wire the Teradata connection manager, handle Teradata JDBC-specific connection behavior, update configuration and Maven dependencies, add unit and mocked integration tests, and document the equivalent import command and setup requirements.

Replace the hard-coded logging path with a configurable property, preserve the existing default, update startup/configuration handling, add tests for custom and default paths, and update installation documentation.

Move message-bus implementation and relevant tests into the Spring Bus repository/module, define or preserve public APIs, update Maven packaging and transitive dependencies, replace XD-local references with the dependency, and verify representative messaging flows.

Move input/output conversion types, registries, adapters, and tests into Spring Cloud Data Flow, expose extension points for custom domain-object conversion, update XD consumers and dependency metadata, and verify standard and custom conversion paths.

activities.activity_name: Extract serialization codecs into Spring Bus
activities.activity_description: Move serialization codec implementations and tests into Spring Bus, preserve serialization compatibility, update package and dependency references, remove duplicated XD code, and validate representative encoded message exchanges.

Design and implement an in-process Admin SPI backed by Module Launcher, including module creation, start, stop, status, failure handling, lifecycle cleanup, configuration, and local pipeline integration tests.

Implement the Receptor-based Admin SPI adapter, including request/authentication configuration, module launch and environment mapping, instance/status handling, shutdown, error translation, retry or timeout behavior, mocked Receptor tests, and deployment documentation.

Evaluate discovery mechanisms and lifecycle integration for self-registering Data Flow modules, define metadata and health semantics, implement a minimal configurable prototype, test registration and deregistration behavior, and produce an implementation recommendation with identified limitations.

Run full builds and focused integration suites across the extracted modules and XD, test compatibility of existing streams and module launchers, investigate and fix regressions, and validate configuration, dependency, packaging, and runtime behavior.

Update user and developer documentation, configuration references, migration notes, sample commands, API/design notes, dependency versions, changelog information, and final packaging or build metadata for the complete increment.
